output:
I'll start by reading the guide and the package layout.

Output was truncated; I'll read the middle files individually.

The rules per command are clear now. I'm saving a copy of the original package so I can compare behaviour afterwards, then writing `access.py`.

Now the six command modules.

That call was cut off before it ran. I'll write the modules as separate files instead.

`show.py` failed with a transient EBUSY error. I'll retry it.

All 3,600 random commands per seed set match the original, byte for byte. To check the fuzzer can detect differences, I'll flip one rule and rerun it.

The fuzzer catches both flipped rules, so its clean result means something. Next, a scan for rule 1 (no access logic outside `access.py`), then the access tests.

Everything left in the command modules is output formatting, the `RULES` keyword names, or prose. `store.py`, `render.py` and `errors.py` are unchanged. I'll write the access tests now.

All tests pass. Writing the status file.

All access checks now live in the new `docshelf/access.py`, and no command changes what it prints, writes or returns. The 32 tests pass with `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` (the existing ones plus the new `tests/test_access.py`). `store.py`, `render.py` and `errors.py` are byte-for-byte unchanged (checked by md5).

I also compared the refactored package against a saved copy of the original. That run used 14,400 random commands over random workspaces, covering every command and option. The workspaces included odd-case and padded role names, blank teams, `*` grants with missing granters, and times exactly on `until` minutes and days. Standard output, standard error, exit status and every workspace file, including `activity.log`, matched byte for byte. Flipping one rule on purpose made the comparison fail, so it does detect differences.

`listing`, `show`, `edit`, `share`, `delete` and `audit` each define a module-level `RULES` and pass it to every call into `access`. The values below are read from each command's code, not from the table in the guide, as the guide says to do:

| Command | roles | suspension | ends | delegation | blank_team | wildcard_admin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `listing` | folded | through | exclusive | all | False | True |
| `show` | folded | through | exclusive | all | True | True |
| `edit` | lower | before | inclusive | owned | False | False |
| `share` | exact | status | exclusive | none | False | False |
| `delete` | exact | status | exclusive | none | False | False |
| `audit` | folded | through | exclusive | none | False | True |

For `share` and `delete`, `blank_team` and `wildcard_admin` never come into play, so those two fields are arbitrary there.

I kept the differences between the old copies as they were, and none are fixed. For example, `edit` accepts a `*` grant from anyone, while `list`, `show` and `audit` trust it only from an admin. `show` is the only command that lets users with no team into documents that have no team.

I wrote the result to `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.

command_result.command: cd /app && git status 2>&1 | head -3; find . -path ./.git -prune -o -type f -print | grep -v __pycache__ | head -100; wc -l docshelf/*.py docs/*.md tests/*.py
cd /app/docshelf && for f in store errors render cli listing show edit share delete audit __init__ __main__; do echo "=== $f"; cat -A $f.py | sed 's/\$$//' ; done; cat ../docs/changelog.md

cd /app/docshelf && sed -n 36,60p edit.py; cat ../tests/test_cli.py ../tests/test_commands.py; ls ../tests/expected | head -3; head -c 600 ../tests/expected/index.json; python --version; cat ../samples/north/*.csv
mkdir -p /tmp/orig && cp -r /app/docshelf /tmp/orig/ && cp -r /app/samples /tmp/orig_samples && cd /app/docshelf && md5sum store.py render.py errors.py > /tmp/md5.txt; cat /tmp/md5.txt

cd /tmp && for s in 1 2 3 4; do python fuzz.py /tmp/orig $s 300 o$s.json & python fuzz.py /app $s 300 n$s.json & done; wait; for s in 1 2 3 4; do cmp o$s.json n$s.json && echo same $s; done; python - <<'E'
import json,collections
d=json.load(open('/tmp/n1.json'))
print(len(d), collections.Counter(str(x[1])+x[0][0] for x in d))
E

cd /tmp && rm -rf mut && mkdir mut && cp -r /app/docshelf mut/ && sed -i 's/ends=access.END_INCLUSIVE/ends=access.END_EXCLUSIVE/' mut/docshelf/edit.py && python fuzz.py /tmp/mut 1 300 m1.json; cmp o1.json m1.json | head -1; sed -i 's/blank_team=True/blank_team=False/' mut/docshelf/show.py; cp /app/docshelf/edit.py mut/docshelf/; python fuzz.py /tmp/mut 2 300 m2.json; cmp o2.json m2.json | head -1

cd /app/docshelf && grep -nE '\.role|\.status|suspended_until|\.grants|\.delegations|granted_by|getattr|vars\(|__dict__|admin|editor|\.owner|\.team|\.level|"role"|"status"' cli.py listing.py show.py edit.py share.py delete.py audit.py; md5sum -c /tmp/md5.txt; python -c "import docshelf.access as a; print([n for n in dir(a) if not n.startswith('_')])"
cd /app && python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -20; find . -name __pycache__ -prune -exec rm -rf {} +; ls samples/north; diff -r samples /tmp/orig_samples && echo samples-unchanged
